weapons.name: MC 14 Tipat
weapons.source_note: Verbatim maker line: "Rifling : Right Hand 6 Unit(250 mm)" (page states "Caliber : .380ACP"). The listed name 'MC 14 Tipat' matches no separate Girsan designation; the .380 ACP Girsan MC 14 is published here as 250 mm / 6 grooves right hand. The MC 14 T tip-up variant has no separately published rifling.

weapons.name: MC 1911 Commander
weapons.source_note: Verbatim maker line for the .45 ACP model: "Rifling : Right Hand 6 Unit(406 mm)" (page states "Caliber : .45 ACP"). The Girsan MC 1911 C Commander page gives the line-range value "Rifling : Right Hand 6 Unit(250-406 mm)" (9x19mm/9mm = 250 mm, .45 ACP = 406 mm); sha256 c2201a59f2612cebc10ef5015f5a785ab865b7161bdee8ed30a305e17808a216, https://girsan.com/products/mc-1911-c-black/3-8-52. .45 ACP value 406 mm taken.

weapons.name: Micro Desert Eagle
weapons.source_note: Verbatim spec: "Barrel : 3.0”, Nickel Teflon, Conventional Rifling, 1 - 16 right-hand twist". 16 in = 406.4 mm. Manual elsewhere says "polygonal rifling" for the M380; no groove count is published.

weapons.name: PP-19 Bizon
weapons.source_note: Barrel: Four-groove with right-hand twist of one turn. In 240 mm (9.4 inches). The bore and chamber are chrome lined.

weapons.name: T3x UPR .300WM
weapons.source_note: Maker spec JSON on the official Tikka page: "rifleCaliber":"300_win_mag", ... "rifleRateOfTwist":"1_10" (label "Rate of Twist", translation "rifleRateOfTwist.1_10":"1:10\""). All .300 Win. Mag. T3x variants on the page read 1_10. 1 in 10 inches = 254.0 mm. Groove count not published.
